subject: Post-call: migration & compatibility priorities + proposed tests
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: migration & compatibility priorities + proposed tests

Tom — great talk earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

Recap (what I heard)
- Primary objective: migrate their conversational search and chat endpoints off current managed service with minimal app changes.
- Top priorities: OpenAI-compatible API surface, streaming parity, embeddings parity for semantic search, predictable latency at 1k tokens, and an option for private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for regulated data.
- Competitive context: AcmeAI is benchmarking against hyperscaler managed endpoints (Vertex/Managed Azure) and evaluating TCO + migration effort.

Proposed tests (we can run these collaboratively)
1) API parity smoke: replace a single API call using OpenAI-compatible endpoint & SDK swap — report errors and diff in tokens/outputs.
2) Latency + streaming: 1k-token generation with streaming; measure tail 95/99 p99 latencies.
3) Embeddings parity: run 500-sample similarity check vs current embeddings; measure drift (cosine) and recall at K.
4) Cost sensitivity: run representative workload (50k tokens/day) with batching/quantization profiles to estimate unit cost.

Attachments I’m dropping into the Drive folder and included here: compat-checklist.xlsx (test checklist), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf (high-level comparison). Marissa will provide SDK swap snippets.

Ask from you: confirm the priority order above and whether we should include a formal data residency check in the smoke test. Also share any timing constraints for the pilot/demo (Tom suggested this week).

Next steps
- If you confirm: we’ll schedule a 45-min technical demo + canary plan with Marissa this Friday.
- I’ll open a HubSpot trial record and share the test folder (links below).

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0112

Thanks, Karthik — that matches my notes. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the test plan: 

- Priority order: 1) API parity (minimal code change), 2) streaming parity (we rely on streaming in product), 3) embeddings parity, 4) cost. Private deployment is a must-have for our regulated customers but can be a later phase (pilot must run in our cloud region first).
- Embeddings: we currently use 1536-dim vectors and have heavy batch indexing jobs — curious how Redwood handles batching for embeddings and memory footprint.
- Quantization: will changes to model variants (e.g., 8-bit/4-bit) impact embedding similarity in ways we should expect?
- Data retention and logs: who has access to inference logs and audit trails in a hosted vs private deployment? We’ll need that documented.

We’re available for a technical demo Friday 09/25 between 10:00–13:00 PDT. If you can get Marissa to show the SDK swap + a short streaming demo that would be ideal.

Tom
Tom Reynolds
Director, Platform Engineering — AcmeAI
tom.reynolds@acmeai.com

Tom — thanks for the clear priorities. A few concrete notes and a minimal SDK/cURL example so your engineers can assess the swap effort quickly. I’ve attached a zip with three example snippets (python, node, curl).

Quick answers:
- Embeddings batching: Redwood supports async batch ingestion for embeddings with configurable batch size; memory footprint is a function of shard size and batch concurrency. We generally advise starting with batch_size=64 and scaling up.
- Quantization effects: for text generation 4-bit quantization can be fine for many models; embeddings are more sensitive — we recommend running an A/B embedding similarity test (we’ll help run this) and default to 8-bit/FP16 for production embeddings unless the drift is negligible.
- Logs & retention: hosted API provides token-level logs and tenant-scoped audit trails; access is RBAC-controlled. Private deployments can ship logs to your KMS/SIEM per your retention policy. I’ll include a short doc in the Drive on what’s accessible in each mode.

SDK swap example (minimal change) — Python pseudo: 

# Current (OpenAI)
import openai
openai.api_key = "${ACME_KEY}"
resp = openai.ChatCompletion.create(model="gpt-2-qa", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize"}])

# Redwood (drop-in compatible)
import requests
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer ${ACME_KEY}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
payload = {"model": "redwood-gpt-2-qa", "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Summarize"}], "stream": false}
resp = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions", json=payload, headers=headers).json()

Notes: default param names and response shapes are highly similar; streaming is a chunked HTTP response compatible with existing SDK patterns. Full code samples (including Node + curl) in sdk-swap-snippets.zip.

Proposed smoke test (we can run together during Friday demo)
- Endpoint parity: 100 sample prompts, compare outputs and token delta.
- Streaming latency: 100 runs at 1k tokens, measure p95/p99.
- Embedding drift: 500-sample recall@10 comparison.

I’ll join Friday’s session and can run the SDK swap live.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
